summary: Wilfried Nölle was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Helmuth von Glasenapp from circa 1946 to 1950.

Wilhelm Alexander Unkrig was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kazan Theological Academy in 1908, he served as a librarian at the Anthropos Institute (1924–1926) and Leiden University (1936), then taught at Goethe University Frankfurt from 1943.

Wilhelm Brandenstein studied at Innsbruck and Vienna under scholars including Kretschmer, Walde, and Trubetzkoy, completing his Ph.D. In linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, he held posts at the University of Graz, serving as institute director from 1941 to 1967.

Wilhelm Cartellieri was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Leipzig and Vienna, completing his Ph.D. in Vienna, and under Georg Bühler. He completed his habilitation at the University of Innsbruck in 1899, where he became an extraordinary professor in 1902.

Wilhelm Deecke studied linguistics and Indology at Leipzig and Berlin under scholars including Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, obtaining his doctorate in Leipzig. He primarily held leadership roles in secondary education, serving as director at Ernestinenschule, Strassburg, Bouxwiller, and Mulhouse.
Wilhelm Dilger was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission from 1880 to 1907 and later held a post at the University of Tübingen in 1910.

Wilhelm Dilthey was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorial posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), the University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Eggers was an Indologist who studied at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, the German Colonial School, and Kiel University, where he completed his Ph.D. between 1924 and 1929 under Friedrich Otto Schrader.
Wilhelm Ferdinand Hüttemann was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg, earning his Ph.D. in 1890.

Wilhelm Filchner worked in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Prussian Military Academy, Berlin, Königsberg, and Munich, he was appointed a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1938.

Wilhelm Gampert was an Indologist who studied under Moriz Winternitz and Otto Stein at the German University in Prague, earning his Ph.D. From 1945 to 1978, he worked as a scientific worker at the Czech Academy of Sciences' Oriental Institute.

Wilhelm Geiger was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranologist who studied under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen. He served as Professor of Comparative Philology at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1891 and as professor at the University of Munich from 1920 to 1924.

Wilhelm Germann worked in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from circa 1858 to 1862 and held a post with the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission in 1864.

Wilhelm Gesenius worked in linguistics and religious studies. After studying at Helmstedt and Göttingen under Thomas Christian Tychsen, he held a post at the University of Göttingen (1806–1809) before serving at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1810 to 1842.

Wilhelm Grube was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg and Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz and Anton Schiefner. He held museum posts and served as an extraordinary professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1884.
Wilhelm Gundert worked in Japanology and religious studies, holding a post at the University of Hamburg from circa 1936 to 1945, where he succeeded Karl Florenz.

Wilhelm Halbfass worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Vienna, Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt, and Hamburg. His main appointments included Brock University (1970–1973) and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a professor from 1982 to 2000.

Wilhelm Havers was a scholar of linguistics and Indology educated at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Bern (1915), Würzburg (1920), Breslau (1929), and Vienna (1937–1953).

Wilhelm Jahn was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Marburg, Rostock, Kiel, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Julius Jolly. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Zurich (1909–1918) and taught at Halle (1918–1919).

Wilhelm K. Essler is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Munich under Wolfgang Stegmüller and Wilhelm Britzelmayr. From circa 1980 to 2005, he served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt.
